newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian parties urge full isolation of Israel.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian parties urge full isolation of Israel.

text.p: Egypt's largest opposition parties, together with the outlawed Moslem Brotherhood, have called for the complete isolation of Israel in retaliation for its policies in Arab East Jerusalem.

In a "Jerusalem Appeal" released on Friday after a meeting on Thursday evening, the parties asked the government to recall the Egyptian ambassador from Tel Aviv, suspend the sale of Egyptian oil to Israel and stop Egyptians travelling to Israel or Israeli tourists coming to Egypt.

The signatories include Wafd Party leader Fouad Serageddin, Labour Party leader Ibrahim Shukri, Tagammu leader Khaled Mohyeddin, Nasserite Party leader Ziaeddin Daoud, Liberal Party leader Mustafa Kamal Murad, Maamoun el-Hodeibi of the Moslem Brotherhood and the leaders of some professional associations.
The parties have only a handful of seats in parliament and the government rarely takes their advice.

"The Egyptian government...is called upon to stop acting on all the economic, commercial and cultural agreements and protocols which it has signed with Israel, to stop selling oil and gas, and to stop Zionist tourism and all shapes of normalisation with Israel," the appeal says.
Egyptian workers should come home from Israel and the government should find alternative work for them, it adds.
Another proposal is that the government freeze all regional economic projects which include Israel and which grew out of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) economic conferences.
The manifesto includes a call for steps against the United States, seen as Israel's ally against the Palestinians.

"(The government is called upon) to take a stand against American penetration of Egyptian society in a way that threatens Egyptian security -- as illustrated recently by the opening in Egypt of a Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) office, which should be closed down immediately," it said.
Arab states, it adds, should boycott this year's MENA conference in the Gulf state of Qatar if the organisers, the World Economic Forum, insist on inviting Israel.
